tagline: Up the river road, between red walls, to Cisco.
intro: From the Colorado River bridge at the north end of Moab, Route 128 goes into the river's gorge and keeps to it for 13 miles, sandstone walls close on either hand and Arches National Park across the water. Moab calls it the river road. Then the gorge opens into Castle and Professor valleys, where Wagon Master and Rio Grande were filmed.

A few miles past the Dewey crossing the road leaves the gorge and runs across open desert toward the Book Cliffs, ending at Interstate 70 near Cisco, an old water stop for steam locomotives. Cisco is the town the highway is signed for, though it never actually enters it.

moments.title: Grandstaff Canyon
moments.text: A trailhead beside the road leads up the canyon of William Grandstaff, who ran cattle here in the late 1870s, to Morning Glory Natural Bridge about 2.5 miles in.

moments.title: Fisher Towers
moments.text: At about mile 24.7 a viewpoint looks over to the Fisher Towers, red spires named for an 1880s miner, standing against the often snow-covered La Sal Mountains.

moments.title: Dewey Bridge
moments.text: Dewey Bridge, a 1916 suspension span with a wooden deck, was the longest in Utah until 2008, when a child playing with matches started the fire that took it.

practical: Parts of the road are narrow, with blind corners and no shoulders, and vehicles over 55,000 pounds gross weight are prohibited on the whole highway.

sources.label: Discover Moab, Upper Colorado River Scenic Byway (U-128)
